prompt: Why does a finite-difference derivative get worse when the step h is extremely small?
answer: The truncation error of (f(x+h) - f(x))/h is about h|f''|/2 and shrinks with h, but f(x+h) - f(x) is computed with a rounding error of about eps|f|, which the division by h amplifies to eps|f|/h. Below h near sqrt(eps), about 1e-8, rounding dominates, and at h = 1e-15 the estimate can be off by tens of percent.
